goal:
Create src/lib/ringMenu.ts so that the EXISTING hand-written test file src/lib/ringMenu.test.ts passes. Do NOT modify the test file — it is the specification.

The module is the pure derivation layer for a radial 'action ring' shown when a student clicks a body region on a 3D patient.

EXPORT 1: export interface RingAction { id: string; label: string; technique: string }
EXPORT 2: export interface RingArm { technique: string; label: string; actionId: string }
EXPORT 3: export function deriveRingArms(actions: RingAction[]): RingArm[]
  - One arm per DISTINCT technique. The FIRST action of each technique in input order wins and supplies actionId.
  - Order arms by the canon ['inspect','palpate','percuss','auscultate']; techniques not in the canon come after, in first-appearance order.
  - Arm label = technique string with its first character upper-cased.
  - Return at most 6 arms. Empty input -> [].
EXPORT 4: export function ringArmOffsets(count: number, radius: number): Array<{ x: number; y: number }>
  - count points evenly spaced on a circle of given radius in SCREEN coordinates (+y down), starting at 12 o'clock (0, -radius) and going clockwise. Clockwise with +y down means the angle for index i is (i / count) * 2*PI and the point is (radius * sin(angle), -radius * cos(angle)).
  - Round x and y to 2 decimal places (avoid -0: normalize -0 to 0). count <= 0 -> [].

Style: pure functions, no imports, no classes, no console. Brief JSDoc on each export.
verify: npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json && npx vitest run src/lib/ringMenu.test.ts
